result.note: Tests India's critical minerals policy timeline, China's share of India's magnet supply, and the partner countries in the February 2026 minerals talks.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's policy push on critical minerals and rare-earths, as reported in February 2026:
items: In 2023, India classified more than 20 minerals as critical to its aim of self-reliance.
The USD 800mn incentive scheme approved in November 2025 targets 6,000 tonnes of permanent magnets annually within three years.
The Union Budget 2026-27 announced Dedicated Rare-Earth Corridors to cluster mining, processing, R&D and manufacturing.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong: the scheme targets 6,000 tonnes of permanent magnets annually within seven years, not three. The rare-earth corridors aim to shorten timelines, ease approvals and give investors predictable infrastructure.
questions.source: In November 2025, it approved an USD 800mn incentive scheme targeting 6,000 tonnes of permanent magnets annually within seven years.

questions.prompt: As reported in February 2026, roughly what share of India's magnets is supplied by China?
questions.explain: China dominates rare-earth processing and supplies nearly 90% of India's magnets. Magnets are central to EVs, renewables, grid storage and defence electronics, which is why India is seeking alternative partners.
questions.source: Today, that supply chain runs largely through China, which dominates rare-earth processing and supplies nearly 90% of India’s magnets.

questions.prompt: In February 2026, India was reported to be in talks to jointly explore, extract, process and recycle lithium and rare-earths with which group of countries?
questions.explain: New Delhi is talking to Brazil, Canada, France and the Netherlands. Brazil and Canada bring mining depth, while France and the Netherlands add processing technology, advanced manufacturing and long-term capital.
questions.source: New Delhi is in talks with Brazil, Canada, France, and Netherlands to jointly explore, extract, process, and recycle lithium and rare-earths.
